The driver's closest approach was 0 m at 08:43:00 [F2] and the vehicle was stationary at 0 m from the pickup from 08:43:00 to 08:51:00 [F4], so the assertion that the driver was not there cannot stand. The rider's own brief concedes this and falls back on the fee-basis argument [C4].

The fee entered under the driver-cancellation branch: the driver cancelled at 08:51:00 [F5], and the only route to a valid no-show charge is NS-1, via NS-0 [F5][NS-0]. The cancellation fee of $5.00 on record [F9] is the case-record parameter standing in for the headline figure, and no other charge appears in the fare record [F10].

NS-1(i) is satisfied on the platform_auto branch: the arrival was auto-confirmed at 08:43:00 with GPS within 10 m, and no manual driver tap appears in this record [F7]. The clause expressly allows platform confirmation, so this satisfies the element rather than escaping it, and nothing supports mislabelling an auto-confirmation as a button press [F6][NS-1]. NS-1(ii) is satisfied: the driver was 0 m from the pickup at the moment of confirmation [F7][F2][NS-1].

NS-1(iii) is satisfied under the case record's own threshold: this record carries a no-show threshold of 8 minutes, reached at 8 min or more, and the driver stayed continuously inside 200 m for 480 s after the 08:43:00 confirmation until the 08:51:00 cancellation [F7][F6][NS-1]. The default over-3-minute figure is displaced by the recorded threshold. The rider's argument that the operator's 5-minute free-wait timer [F8] makes the fee unlawful must fail: free wait time is the waiting-charge start point, not the no-show threshold, and NS-1 forbids substituting it into (iii) [F8][NS-1].

Continuity of the wait is documented, not inferred: sampling is about every 3 min with a gap counting as a hole only beyond 6 min, and the 8-minute stationary dwell at 0 m is covered by valid samples [F1][F4][NS-1]. The chat record is complete with every message timestamped [F16], and the driver's four messages and one 22-second unanswered call against zero rider messages document reasonable contact attempts during the wait [F11][F12][F13][F14][F15][F17][NS-1].

No NS-2 failure is shown, so no refund is triggered: (i), (ii) and (iii) all hold and the driver's recorded position was inside the pickup radius at the moment of the arrival confirmation [F7][F3][NS-2]. The profile facts decide nothing on either side and are not relied on for the outcome [F21][F22][NS-1]; the RD-6 flag_account condition is not met because no violation is upheld against the driver here [F22][RD-6].

Amount: the disputed item is the $5.00 cancellation fee [F9]; because no NS-1 element fails there is no refundable portion, so the refundable amount is nil and amount is null under no_action [F9][NS-1]. The rider's remedy, if she still contests the fee, is the NS-7 in-app waiver review within 30 days, which is a Ryde discretionary route, not an automatic refund [NS-7].

Safety screen: I read every chat line, the complaint and the driver's statements. The messages are ordinary pickup coordination: an arrival announcement, a car description and plate, a chase-up question, and a notice of intent to cancel [F11][F12][F14][F15]. The message that the driver will otherwise have to cancel the trip [F15] is a statement of intent about the trip, not a threat, and no intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation appears anywhere in the record [F13]. Finding: none.

claims.assertion: The $5.00 charged to the rider is a cancellation/no-show fee, and the driver cancelled at 08:51:00 while the platform had recorded his arrival at 08:43:00; under NS-0 the fee can only stand if the driver's no-show claim satisfies NS-1.

NS-1(i) is satisfied only as a platform auto-confirmation, not a driver button press: the arrival at 08:43:00 was auto-confirmed by GPS within 10 m with the driver 0 m from the pickup point, and the record nowhere shows a driver 'I'm Here' tap — the rule must be applied as written, on the platform_auto branch.

The rider's case rests on the platform's own wait timer: the timer started 08:43:10, the free period expired at 08:48:10, and the fee was applied at 08:51:00 — the operator itself charged a 5-minute 'no-show' style fee, not a >3-minute waiting fee, so NS-1(iii)'s default 'over 3 minutes' threshold is not shown to have been the basis of the charge.

The rider's complaint that she was present at the pickup point while the driver was not is contradicted by the system record: the driver was stationary 0 m from the pickup from 08:43:00 to 08:51:00, so no claim can be built on her presence-at-the-lobby statement (system records win over statements).

No GPS hole arises during the wait: sampling is about every 3 minutes and a gap counts only beyond 6 minutes, and the driver's dwell at 0 m is continuously recorded — so the continuity requirement of NS-1(iii) is not defeated by missing data.

The driver made four contact attempts (arrival message 08:43, second message 08:45, a 22-second unanswered call at 08:47, and further messages at 08:49 and 08:50) while the rider sent none; the chat record is complete with every message timestamped, so the driver's waiting is documented and the rider cannot rely on a communication failure.

The rider seeks reversal only if the fee cannot be sustained under NS-1: on this record the driver's arrival radius, stationary wait and advance notice are all documented, so the fee is not vulnerable to NS-2 and the appropriate rider-side fallback is a waiver request reviewed humanly rather than an automatic refund.
No safety-trigger appears on the record: the messages contain no threat, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation, so SAFE-1/SAFE-2 escalation is not invoked by either side.

The driver has one dispute on record, none upheld, and the rider has four disputes with one upheld, none of them no-show; nothing in the profiles supports a driver flag_account request in this case, and profile facts cannot decide it anyway.

weaknesses: The strongest fact against the rider is F4/F2: the GPS record shows the driver stationary 0 m from the pickup for the full 8 minutes before cancellation, which directly contradicts the complaint's assertion that 'the driver was not' at the pickup point — the system record governs under the evidence hierarchy.

F7 shows the arrival was auto-confirmed within 10 m at 08:43:00 and F3 shows 10 minutes cumulative within 200 m, so NS-1(i)/(ii) and the default >3-minute continuity in NS-1(iii) are met by the driver; the rider cannot show any NS-1 element failed.
F11–F17 show four driver messages and one call with zero rider responses, which undermines any argument that the rider was present and reachable at the lobby.

The rider's own filing is inconsistent with F6/F8: she says she waited 10 minutes but the record shows the operator's free period expired at 08:48:10 and the fee was applied at 08:51:00, on a 5-minute timer rather than the NS-1 3-minute default; the 5-minute free-wait figure is a waiting-charge start point, not a no-show threshold (NS-1), so it cannot by itself convert the fee into an unlawful charge.
The cancellation fee on record is $5.00 (F9), not the $6.61 headline figure in NS-0/NS-7, so any refund argument pinned to the $6.61 voucher amount is mis-sized and must be avoided.

claims.assertion: The driver did reach the pickup point: GPS shows a closest approach of 0 m to the pickup at 08:43:00 and the vehicle stationary at 0 m from the pickup from 08:43:00 to 08:51:00 — the rider's claim that 'the driver never showed up' is contradicted by the system record.

Arrival was confirmed at 08:43:00 with the GPS within 10 m of the pickup point, i.e. well inside the 200 m arrival radius; this was a platform auto-confirmation, not a driver button press, so the record should be read as 'platform_auto' as recorded.

After arrival confirmation the driver remained within 200 m of the pickup for 8 min 0 s continuously until cancellation at 08:51:00, so the requirement of waiting more than 3 minutes (≥ 3:01) after arrival is satisfied; the record's own wait timer expired 5 min 0 s of free waiting at 08:48:10 and the fee was applied at 08:51:00.

Cumulative time within 200 m of the pickup before cancellation was 10 min 0 s, first entering that radius at 08:41:00, which corroborates continuous attendance at the pickup rather than a brief or absent presence.

The chat shows the driver announced arrival at the lobby at 08:43, gave the car description and plate at 08:45, called the rider at 08:47 (outgoing call rang 22 s, unanswered), and asked at 08:49 and 08:50 whether the rider was coming — four driver messages and one unanswered call with zero rider replies, so the rider was not responsive to reasonable contact attempts.

The chat record is complete — 5 messages, every one timestamped — so there is no evidence gap that would force the case to manual review (no missing-timestamp hole) and the driver's conduct can be assessed on the full record.

The GPS sampling interval in this record is about 3 min 0 s and a gap counts as a hole only beyond 6 min 0 s, so the 8-min stationary period is covered by continuous valid samples; the wait cannot be dismissed as an inference between sparse readings.

Cancellation was made by the driver at 08:51:00 after the waiting threshold was met, and the $5.00 fee on record is the charge in dispute; the driver asks that it stand. Nothing in the record raises a safety, threat or dangerous-driving issue requiring escalation.

The driver's profile (2.5 years, 4.9 rating, 3201 trips, 1 dispute with 0 upheld) supports denying the rider's complaint, and the rider's profile (rating 3.9, 4 disputes, 1 upheld) is context only; no flag_account action is sought because there is no upheld violation here.

weaknesses: The driver cancelled instead of completing the trip, so this is a no-show cancellation case under NS-1 rather than a completed-trip waiting-fee case under NS-6; if the judge reads NS-6's 'continues the trip' condition as governing the $5.00, the rider's framing could be preferred (F5, F9, NS-6).

The record shows no rider messages and no rider-side location evidence at the lobby, so the rider's account that they were present cannot be independently confirmed from the file — the strongest support for the driver is the absence of contact, not positive proof of the rider's absence (F17, F21).

The fee amount on record is $5.00 (F9) while NS-0/NS-1 speak of a $6.61 cancellation fee, so if the judge applies NS-1 literally the fee basis is a mismatch; the honest position is that $5.00 is what was charged and what the driver asks be retained (F5, F9).

The driver's own message at 08:50 says 'otherwise I'll have to cancel the trip' (F15), which the rider may characterise as a threat to cancel rather than a genuine no-show cancellation, though the GPS record shows the waiting precondition was in fact satisfied (F4, F6, F7).

points.response: Conceded as to the GPS record: F2 and F4 do show 0 m at 08:43:00 and a stationary 8-minute dwell at 0 m, which is why our brief (C4) reserved itself to the record and did not build the rider's case on her 'driver never showed up' statement.
Not contested: F7 records the arrival as platform auto-confirmation, and our C2 asked only that it be read as auto and not mislabelled as a driver 'I'm Here' press under NS-1(i).

The 8 min 0 s dwell inside 200 m satisfies NS-1(iii) on its face, but the same facts show the operator applied a 5-minute free-wait timer (F8), a waiting-charge start point and not the NS-1 threshold; the rider's complaint that she was charged a 'no-show' fee she was never shown to have triggered is therefore a fee-basis question under NS-1 read with F8, not a claim that the driver was absent.

Accepted as a GPS fact: F3 shows the driver first within 200 m at 08:41:00 and 10 min 0 s cumulative inside 200 m, which corroborates attendance and leaves the rider's only viable ground as the fee basis, not presence.

The contact log in F11–F15 and F17 is what it is, but four messages and one unanswered call do not show the rider was absent from the lobby — the file contains no rider-side location fact at all, and NS-1 requires positive GPS evidence of the driver's own position and wait, which the driver has, while nothing in NS-1 makes rider silence an element of the charge.

Agreed that the chat is complete and timestamped (F16), so no G12-style manual referral arises from missing timestamps; completeness of the chat simply means the fee must be tested on NS-1's own elements, and those elements are met only on the operator's own 5-minute timer in F8.
Not contested: F1 (3-minute sampling, hole only beyond 6 minutes) read with F4 means the wait period is covered by valid samples, matching our own C5.

The driver's 08:50 message 'otherwise I'll have to cancel the trip' (F15) is a statement of intent, not a threat within SAFE-1, so no escalation is sought on it; but if the fee is to stand it must be the fee NS-1 authorises, and F9's $5.00 is not shown to be computed under NS-1's default threshold when F8 applies a 5-minute free period instead.

Profiles cut both ways and decide nothing (F21, F22): the rider's four disputes with none no-show do not establish this charge, and the driver's clean history cannot cure a fee applied on a timer the record does not tie to NS-1's threshold.

The rider does not press for automatic reversal of a record-consistent charge: on F3/F4/F6 the NS-1 elements are documented, so the rider falls back to NS-7's human waiver review of the $5.00 charge rather than asking this tribunal to void it.

Agreed on the route into the policy: the fee can stand only if NS-1 is satisfied, and it is — the driver was within 200 m at the moment of arrival confirmation and stayed there 8 min 0 s before cancelling (F3, F4, F6, F7), so NS-0's NS-1 branch is met, not defeated.

I agree and my brief already states the arrival was a platform auto-confirmation (F7), not a driver tap — NS-1(i) expressly allows 'or the platform automatically confirms arrival', so the platform_auto branch satisfies the element rather than escaping it.

The 5-minute figure is not the no-show threshold on this record, and NS-1 says exactly that: the free-wait time is the waiting-charge start point and the mid-trip timer fields (F8) cannot be substituted for the (iii) test; (iii) is measured from arrival confirmation to cancellation, which here is 8 min 0 s (F6, F7), exceeding the >3-minute default.

This is the rider's own concession and it is decisive: F4 puts the vehicle stationary 0 m from the pickup for the entire 8 minutes before cancellation, so the complaint's assertion that the driver never showed up cannot stand against the system record.

Accepted — F1 sets the hole threshold at over 6 minutes against a ~3-minute sampling interval, so the 08:43:00–08:51:00 dwell in F4 is continuously documented and NS-1(iii) is not defeated by missing data.

Accepted and it confirms my case: four driver messages and one 22-second unanswered call against zero rider messages (F11–F15, F17), with a complete timestamped chat record (F16), so there is no communication gap and no missing-record escalation.

The rider's own fallback concedes the point in dispute: she seeks reversal 'only if the fee cannot be sustained under NS-1', and on this record every NS-1 element is documented (F3, F4, F6, F7), so the fee is sustained and the outcome is no_action; there is no NS-2 failure to trigger a refund.
Agreed — no message in the record contains a threat, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation (F11, F12, F14, F15), so SAFE-1/SAFE-2 escalation is not invoked by either side.
Agreed, and I do not seek flag_account: the driver has one dispute with none upheld (F22) and this case produces no upheld violation, so no account action arises and the profiles decide nothing.
